name: Lost Relic Carry

angles.text: As a dwarf, you share your people's drive to unearth ancient relics from their makers. This fragment is a prized find for dwarven heritage.
As an engineer, you can see how the rock-mech's composite material and intricate design point to mechanical principles beyond standard mortal engineering.

faq.answer: The Titan Relic is a fractured piece of an ancient rock-mech automaton. Its unknown composite formed part of an intricate mechanical device.
Prospector Whelgar is a dwarven researcher who oversees the excavation site in the Wetlands. He studies ancient earthen remains and relics uncovered across the region.
Bring the relic to Prospector Whelgar at his excavation site in the Wetlands. There, dwarven excavators investigate ancient ruins.
faq.q: Where does the relic need to be delivered?

faq.answer: The fragment is identified as a Titan relic. Dwarven lore ties ancient mechanical constructs and stone automatons to the enigmatic Titans who shaped the world.
Whelgar respects the danger of reaching the depths where these automatons lie. He says surviving the delve and returning with an intact piece earns genuine respect.
faq.q: Why does Prospector Whelgar treat the relic with reverence?

faq.answer: The automaton's material is an unfamiliar composite, unlike ordinary stone or forged metal. It shows the sophisticated craft of ancient Titan constructs.
faq.q: What is unusual about the automaton's material?

sections.body: A rock-mech has left behind a fractured piece of its ancient craft. Its unfamiliar composite marks it as part of a sophisticated mechanism tied to the Titans.
sections.title: A Fragment of Ancient Craft

sections.body: Prospector Whelgar studies ancient remains at the Wetlands excavation site. Bring the relic safely to him, and dwarven scholars will have physical evidence for their study of their ancient heritage.
sections.title: Delivery to the Excavation

summary: You carry a broken rock-mech relic through the Wetlands toward Prospector Whelgar. Its strange material draws the eye of dwarven researchers.
